deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether the Dataproc Session Template can be destroyed or removed from Terraform management. This affects resource availability and protection against unintended destructive lifecycle operations.

labels.description:
The labels to associate with this session template.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels are descriptive key-value metadata used to organize the session template. They are not security controls and are not a useful platform security policy target.

location.description: The location in which the session template will be created in.
location.rationale: Determines the region where the Session Template is created. A platform security policy can restrict deployment to approved regions to support data residency and regional security requirements.

name.description:
The resource name of the session template in the following format:
projects/{project}/locations/{location}/sessionTemplates/{template_id}
name.rationale: Identifies the Dataproc Session Template resource. Resource names and identifiers are not useful platform security policy targets.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifies the Google Cloud project containing the Session Template. It is a resource reference and is not itself a useful platform security policy target.

environment_config.description: Environment configuration for the session execution.

environment_config.execution_config.idle.description:
The duration to keep the session alive while it's idling.
Exceeding this threshold causes the session to terminate. Minimum value is 10 minutes; maximum value is 14 day.
Defaults to 1 hour if not set. If both ttl and idleTtl are specified for an interactive session, the conditions
are treated as OR conditions: the workload will be terminated when it has been idle for idleTtl or when ttl has
been exceeded, whichever occurs first.
environment_config.execution_config.idle.rationale: Controls how long an idle session remains active before termination. This is a workload lifecycle and resource-management setting rather than a platform security control.

environment_config.execution_config.kms_.description: The Cloud KMS key to use for encryption.
environment_config.execution_config.kms_.rationale: Encryption keys require a policy to ensure they are set and customer-managed. The policy should require the key to be non-empty without pinning a specific key.

environment_config.execution_config.netw.description: Tags used for network traffic control.
environment_config.execution_config.netw.rationale: Associates the workload with network traffic-control tags. The tags are network configuration references chosen by the deployment architecture rather than direct platform security policy targets.

environment_config.execution_config.serv.description: Service account that used to execute workload.
environment_config.execution_config.serv.rationale: Controls the identity used to execute the workload. Requiring an explicitly selected service account supports least-privilege workload identity and avoids reliance on an unintended default identity.

environment_config.execution_config.stag.description:
A Cloud Storage bucket used to stage workload dependencies, config files, and store
workload output and other ephemeral data, such as Spark history files. If you do not specify a staging bucket,
Cloud Dataproc will determine a Cloud Storage location according to the region where your workload is running,
and then create and manage project-level, per-location staging and temporary buckets.
This field requires a Cloud Storage bucket name, not a gs://... URI to a Cloud Storage bucket.
environment_config.execution_config.stag.rationale: Identifies the Cloud Storage bucket used to stage workload files and temporary data. This is a resource reference; the bucket itself is the security control target rather than the pointer stored in this argument.

environment_config.execution_config.subn.rationale: Identifies the network resource used for workload execution. It is a pointer to a subnetwork rather than a direct platform security policy target.

environment_config.execution_config.ttl.description:
The duration after which the workload will be terminated.
When the workload exceeds this duration, it will be unconditionally terminated without waiting for ongoing
work to finish. If ttl is not specified for a session workload, the workload will be allowed to run until it
exits naturally (or run forever without exiting). If ttl is not specified for an interactive session,
it defaults to 24 hours. If ttl is not specified for a batch that uses 2.1+ runtime version, it defaults to 4 hours.
Minimum value is 10 minutes; maximum value is 14 days. If both ttl and idleTtl are specified (for an interactive session),
the conditions are treated as OR conditions: the workload will be terminated when it has been idle for idleTtl or
when ttl has been exceeded, whichever occurs first.
environment_config.execution_config.ttl.rationale: Controls the maximum workload lifetime before termination. This is an operational lifecycle setting rather than a direct platform security control.

environment_config.execution_config.auth.description: Authentication configuration for a workload is used to set the default identity for the workload execution.
Authentication type for the user workload running in containers. Possible values: ["SERVICE_ACCOUNT", "END_USER_CREDENTIALS"]
environment_config.execution_config.auth.rationale: Controls how user workloads authenticate during execution. Authentication method is security-relevant because a platform policy can require managed service-account authentication and disallow weaker or less controlled credential methods.

environment_config.peripherals_config.description: Peripherals configuration that workload has access to.

environment_config.peripherals_config.me.description: Resource name of an existing Dataproc Metastore service.
environment_config.peripherals_config.me.rationale: Identifies an existing Dataproc Metastore service used by the workload. This is a reference to another resource rather than a direct platform security policy target.

environment_config.peripherals_config.sp.description: The Spark History Server configuration for the workload.
Resource name of an existing Dataproc Cluster to act as a Spark History Server for the workload.
environment_config.peripherals_config.sp.rationale: Identifies an existing Dataproc Cluster used as a Spark History Server. This is a reference to another resource rather than a direct platform security policy target.

jupyter_session.description: Jupyter configuration for an interactive session.

jupyter_session.display_name.description: Display name, shown in the Jupyter kernelspec card.
jupyter_session.display_name.rationale: Sets the display name shown for the Jupyter session. This is presentation metadata and is not a security control.

jupyter_session.kernel.description: Kernel to be used with Jupyter interactive session. Possible values: ["PYTHON", "SCALA"]
jupyter_session.kernel.rationale: Selects the Jupyter kernel used by the interactive session. This determines the workload programming environment but is not itself a platform security policy target.

runtime_config.description: Runtime configuration for the session template.

runtime_config.container_image.description: Optional custom container image for the job runtime environment. If not specified, a default container image will be used.
runtime_config.container_image.rationale: Controls the container image used for the workload runtime. The image determines the software executed by the workload, so a platform policy can require images to come from approved trusted sources.

runtime_config.properties.description: A mapping of property names to values, which are used to configure workload execution.
runtime_config.properties.rationale: Runtime properties are free-form configuration values used to customize workload execution. A generic platform policy cannot meaningfully constrain arbitrary property names and values without being overly broad, so this argument is not a useful platform policy target.

runtime_config.version.rationale: Selects the session runtime version. Runtime version is a vendor-supported software choice and is not, by itself, a useful platform security policy target.

spark_connect_session.description: Spark connect configuration for an interactive session.
